answer: Each account must lock a bond before it can route payments or vote, while randomly chosen unrelated agents cross-check behavior. If accounts collude to fake support, the protocol slashes their bonds and erases their trust history. Thus a new vertex cannot quickly impersonate a reliable plume publisher or whisper relay. A Sybil attacker must finance every identity, risk every deposit, and repeat costly honest work, so thousands of accounts multiply capital at risk instead of influence.
